title: The weighted vertical projection realization conjecture for alternating sign matrices
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n)$ be a vector of positive integers such that

$$
(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n)\preceq (n,n-1,\ldots,2,1).
$$

Here, an **alternating sign matrix** (ASM) is an $n\times n$ matrix with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$ in which the nonzero entries in every row and column alternate and begin and end with $1$. The weighted vertical projection is the vector obtained by taking the weighted sum of the entries in each column, using the row indices as weights. **Weighted vertical projection realization conjecture.** There exists an $n\times n$ ASM whose weighted vertical projection is $(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n)$. The conjecture proposes a characterization of the possible weighted vertical projections of ASMs; the surrounding discussion presents this as a step toward characterizing the entries of ASHM Latin squares. The source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
source_name: Richard A. Brualdi and Geir Dahl, “Alternating Sign Matrices and Hypermatrices, and a Generalization of Latin Square”, arXiv:1704.07752 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.07752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).
